fields.description_1:
Sodrive needs to help learner drivers compare lesson options before they are ready to book. Packages, pricing, exam preparation and practical information all matter, but they answer different questions at different stages. If every detail appears at once, a first-time learner may struggle to understand which lesson route fits and what to do next.

The website therefore needed a sequence from orientation to package comparison and booking or contact. Instructor and exam information had to support the choice without burying the main actions. On mobile, prices, cards and forms need an order. The portfolio story also had to avoid claims about pass rates, lesson speed or guaranteed driving outcomes. The challenge was to make a driving-school offer easy to compare without oversimplifying the learning process.
fields.description_2:
I organised Sodrive around the decisions a learner makes before booking. Lesson types and packages provide the first comparison, followed by pricing, exam information and practical details that help someone understand what the route involves. Booking and contact actions appear after that context instead of being repeated without explanation.

Instructor information supports trust but does not replace the details of the lesson offer. On smaller screens, package cards, prices and next steps keep a predictable reading order. I used direct labels so new drivers do not need to understand driving-school terminology before choosing a route. The portfolio case now describes the actual WordPress booking journey while avoiding unsupported claims about pass rates, learning speed, exam success or commercial performance.

fields.description_1:
Autoinkoopatlas serves car owners who want to sell a vehicle and need to understand what happens before they submit their details. A seller may want a valuation, information about the selling process or reassurance about the handover. If the website asks for vehicle data before explaining the steps, the form can feel disconnected from the service.

The site therefore needed to connect trust information, the selling process and vehicle intake in an order. Visitors should know what details are required and why before moving toward a valuation or contact request. On mobile, form fields and supporting information need to stay easy to scan. The portfolio story also had to avoid promising a sale price, instant purchase or timing that depends on the vehicle and market.
fields.description_2:
I structured Autoinkoopatlas around the seller's journey from orientation to vehicle submission. The site explains the selling steps and relevant trust information before asking for the details needed for a valuation or follow-up. Vehicle intake stays connected to the process rather than appearing as an isolated form with no context.

Supporting information sits beside the questions it helps answer, and the mobile layout keeps form fields, explanations and actions in a clear sequence. I avoided wording that implies a guaranteed offer, purchase price or completion time because those depend on the car and live market conditions. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress can guide a car owner through a structured selling request without relying on generic automotive claims or invented business outcomes.

fields.description_1:
Boekhoudsnel has to make bookkeeping services understandable to entrepreneurs who may be comparing packages as well as individual tasks. Bookkeeping, tax work and annual accounts often belong together, but a visitor still needs to know what is included and when a package or direct conversation is appropriate. Financial jargon can make that comparison harder.

The website therefore needed to combine service explanations with package information in a way that stays clear on mobile. Pricing or inclusions had to support the decision without implying guaranteed savings, tax results or compliance. Contact actions should follow enough context for a useful conversation. The portfolio problem was to organise an accounting offer around business questions, while avoiding vague expertise claims and unverified outcomes about profit, efficiency or customer growth.
fields.description_2:
I organised Boekhoudsnel around the accounting tasks an entrepreneur is likely to recognise first, then connected them to package information where comparison is useful. Bookkeeping, tax work and annual accounts each have clear explanations, while packages show how recurring support can be grouped without hiding the underlying services.

Contact actions remain available for questions that do not fit a standard package. I used plain wording and kept financial claims measured, avoiding promises about savings, tax positions or business performance. On mobile, service sections, package details and enquiry actions follow a predictable order. The portfolio case now explains how WordPress supports a packaged accounting service without turning the project into generic finance marketing or claiming outcomes that depend on each client's records and circumstances.

fields.description_1:
Voltworks combines electrical work with energy services such as charging and solar. A customer may know the desired result but not which service is involved, so a service list would make the first decision harder. Projects can help explain the work without implying identical requirements.

The website therefore needed to separate electrical, charging and solar-related routes while keeping advice or quotation access clear. Detail had to appear after the service choice instead of overwhelming the introduction. On mobile, service cards and contact actions needed a compact hierarchy. The portfolio story also had to avoid guarantees about energy savings, system performance or installation outcomes. The challenge was to make several technical services understandable without simplifying away the need for site-specific assessment.
fields.description_2:
I structured Voltworks around the type of technical question a customer brings to the site. Electrical work, charging and solar-related solutions have separate routes, each with the practical context needed before a visitor requests advice or a quotation. Project information supports those services without being used as a promise that another property will need the same solution.

The hierarchy keeps deeper technical detail available after the first choice, while contact actions remain visible at natural decision points. On smaller screens, service cards, supporting information and enquiry buttons follow the same order. The portfolio case now presents Voltworks as a multi-service electrical and energy business, avoiding unsupported claims about savings, capacity, payback, installation speed or performance that require property-specific evidence.

fields.description_1:
Jouwgroenteboer is a WooCommerce grocery shop where customers may browse fruit and vegetables by habit or need. Product freshness is important to the business, but the webshop still has to help people find items, understand quantities and move into the cart without making every product page feel identical.

The site therefore needed clear produce categories, useful product detail and straightforward quantity or cart actions. Mobile shopping matters because grocery orders are often built quickly and across many items, so navigation cannot rely on large text blocks. The portfolio story also had to avoid unsupported promises about freshness, stock, delivery or health benefits. The challenge was to make a simple online grocery journey efficient and readable while keeping product information specific enough to support a purchase.
fields.description_2:
I organised Jouwgroenteboer around fast category discovery and repeatable product decisions. Fruit, vegetables and related produce groups give shoppers a clear starting point, while product pages provide the quantity, price and relevant details needed before adding an item to the cart. The shopping path stays consistent so customers do not have to relearn controls for each product.

On mobile, category links, product cards, quantity choices and cart actions keep a compact order that supports building a larger grocery basket. I avoided claims about freshness, delivery time or health effects that require separate evidence. The portfolio case now explains how WooCommerce supports a practical produce shop with quick browsing and purchasing, rather than relying on generic ecommerce language or invented sales and customer outcomes.
